user.title: smartENERGY electricity price helper
user.description: Fetches the tariff prices from smartENERGY (smartTIMES or smartCONTROL). No API key is required.

data_description.tariff: smartTIMES: time-based tariff. smartCONTROL: linked to the EPEX spot market price; a handling fee of 1.2 ct/kWh net (1.44 ct/kWh gross) is added on top.
data_description.include_vat: Affects all sensors of the integration, not just one. "On" (gross, as delivered by the API) is the right choice for the Energy Dashboard and for comparing against your electricity bill.
data_description.grid_zone: Determines the grid fees (grid level 7, quarter-hourly metering) in the total price. "No grid area" leaves them out.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the smartENERGY API.
error.timeout: The smartENERGY API timed out. This usually points to a temporary network or load issue – please try again later.
error.api_rejected: The smartENERGY API rejected the request. The selected tariff is currently unavailable – please try again later.
error.invalid_response: The smartENERGY API returned an unexpected response. This suggests the API's format has changed – please file an issue in the integration's GitHub repository.

abort.single_instance_allowed: smartENERGY is already configured. The API returns the same prices for everyone, so a second instance is not possible. You can change tariff, VAT and grid zone via “Configure” on the existing entry.

user.title: Add cheap-hour sensor
user.description: Create a sensor for one appliance. It is on while the current hour is among the cheapest of the day.

data.name: Name (e.g. boiler, wallbox)
data.exact_hours: Keep the number of hours exact

data_description.cheap_hours: With smartTIMES this has no effect: as a time-based tariff it only has three price tiers of 8 hours each, so any setting between 0.25 h and 8 h yields the same 8 hours. With smartCONTROL the number of hours matters directly, since prices there change almost every quarter-hour. At a tie, the actual on-time can exceed the configured number of hours unless "Keep the number of hours exact" is enabled — in "Consecutive block" mode it is always exact.
data_description.cheap_mode: "Cheapest individual hours": the cheapest quarter-hours of the day — they may be spread across the day (e.g. boiler, wallbox). "Consecutive block": a single cheapest window in one piece — for appliances with a fixed run time that must not be interrupted (washing machine, dishwasher).
data_description.exact_hours: By default, further times that cost exactly as much as the most expensive selected one are also marked cheap — the sensor is then on longer than configured, but never at a higher price. When enabled, it delivers exactly the configured number of hours. Only affects "Cheapest individual hours".

reconfigure.description: Edit the settings of this cheap-hour sensor. It is on while the current hour is among the cheapest of the day.

tariff_data_outdated.title: Tariff data outdated (as of {data_year})
tariff_data_outdated.description: The grid fees and renewable energy surcharge bundled with this version are "as of {data_year}" – these rates are redetermined every year. Since the current calendar year has already moved on, the integration may now be calculating with outdated values. Please update to a newer version of the integration once one with refreshed rates is released.

fetch_failing.title: Tariff prices have not been refreshed for a while
fetch_failing.description: Fetching current tariff prices from the smartENERGY API has been failing for several hours. The integration keeps using the last successfully loaded, cached prices in the meantime – these may by now be outdated. The issue resolves itself automatically once fetching succeeds again.
